To UK Anons: Please describe to me what brought on Brexit? and why the EU will not leave you alone? Links would be nice to get up to speed on what is happening.

Brexit is very complex and after 3 long years the British public wants it to go away. Here's a summary:

  • The UK held a public referendum on EU membership in 2016, as it was promised by the Conservative government in the 2015 election for political purposes. Remain was expected to win but Leave won narrowly (52% vs 48%)

  • The UK Conservative government then began the Leave process. However, because the referendum was conducted on simple remain/leave terms, nobody ever clarified what kind of exit would happen and what is most desirable. There is simply no consensus on this, either among the general public or politicians who represent them.

  • The logical thing to do (and what most pro-Leave public figures promised) would be to negotiate a good exit deal with the EU, which ensures a smooth leave process and doesn't fuck up the UK economy. Leaving without a deal in place ("No Deal Brexit") is potentially very harmful and negative, as most of our trade is with Europe, and if we don't have a trade deal in place when leaving then we will most likely enter recession and serious economic downturn. There is also no majority support for No Deal Brexit, either in Parliament or the general public.

  • It has proved impossible to secure a deal with the EU that pleases everyone. Theresa May (Prime Minister from 2016-19) did negotiate a withdrawal agreement, but it was weak and both sides hated it for different reasons and it couldn't get a majority in Parliament (any withdrawal agreement has to be passed by a majority of MPs).

  • May eventually resigned a few months ago after failing repeatedly to get her deal passed and losing all credibility and control over her own party (which is split between rival Brexit factions). As her deal failed to pass and there is no other deal forthcoming, the UK is currently set to leave the EU on 31st October 2019 without any trade or legal deal, which the majority of the public do not want and which most experts agree will seriously fuck up the UK economy.

  • Boris Johnson replaced her as PM. Johnson is a complex figure - power-hungry and willing to do or say anything to get what he wants. Very popular within his own party, but widely ridiculed and despised by many others. Johnson's strategy has been to push through a No-Deal Brexit (i.e. run the clock down until the end of October) through some quite deceptive and undemocratic measures that sideline Parliament, and then immediately call a new general election when it is too late to stop.

  • Johnson's thinking is that if he pushes no-deal Brexit through, even if it has some negative effects the public will be happy to finally put Brexit behind them and vote for him. He will then have a free-hand to implement his political agenda, which currently looks like a hard-right vision of low corporate taxes, reduced regulations, cutting worker rights, etc.

  • Johnson has failed miserably so far. Parliament united to stop him (including many of his own Conservative MPs, who are now being purged from the party) and have passed a bill this week that effectively outlaws No Deal Brexit. It's not clear what will happen next as events are so dramatic and moving so quickly, but right now he looks to have seriously miscalculated. He will have his hands tied and the opposition parties didn't fall for his trick.

  • The most likely next step is the EU providing an extension for Brexit beyond 31st October (probably to January next year at the earliest) immediately followed by a general election in November. The outcome of that election will determine the future of Brexit, but both the Conservatives and Labour will feel they can win if they get their campaign messages right. Either way, it will be a nasty and divisive election for a country that is sick of politics (this will be the 3rd election in 4 years).
